bus.via: Aéroport Terminal 1 to Gare SNCF Cannes

trips.route_note: Take a direct TER train from Nice-Ville to Cannes-La Bocca or Cannes station, about 35 to 45 minutes, then walk to the seafront Croisette.
trips.why: The train takes about 20 minutes from Nice-Ville and runs 16 times a day, far faster than the 1h 14m bus.
know: The Croisette seafront is the main draw and is an easy walk from the station.
Expect large crowds and higher hotel prices during the Cannes Film Festival in May.

trips.route_note: Take a regular TER train from Nice-Ville toward Cannes or Menton; it takes about 15 to 20 minutes to Antibes station, then a short walk into the old town.
trips.tour_query: Antibes and Cannes day trip from Nice
trips.why: The train takes about 11 minutes and runs 33 times a day, with the old town a short walk from the station.
know: The old town and ramparts are the main sights, and the Picasso museum is housed in the Château Grimaldi.
Trains run frequently, so no advance planning is needed.

trips.route_note: Regional TER trains run from Nice-Ville to Monaco-Monte-Carlo in about 20 minutes, and the station is a short walk or lift ride from the casino and harbor.
trips.why: The train is far faster than the 47-minute bus and drops you a short walk from the casino and harbor.
know: Trains run about 14 times a day from Nice-Ville.
Monaco-Monte-Carlo station is a short walk or lift ride from the casino and harbor.

trips.route_note: Take a regular TER train from Nice-Ville toward Ventimiglia; it takes about 35 to 45 minutes to Menton station, then a short walk up to the old town and basilica.
trips.why: The train takes about 27 minutes and runs 16 times a day, dropping you a short walk from the old town and basilica.
know: It is a quieter, more relaxed town, best suited to visitors who want a slower day.
The Fête du Citron (lemon festival) in February is a well-known reason to visit.
